blocks.note: surface reading: burglars weighing up premises before a break-in
setter's reading: thin sheets that wrap round hand-rolled smokes, joints being cannabis cigarettes

explanation.walkthrough: To case a joint is criminal slang for scouting a place to rob; here case means enclose and joints are rolled smokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin gummed sheets are wrapped around tobacco or cannabis when rolling, so they literally form the outer casing of a joint.

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of glamorous journeys through outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap of time or distance between two things is a space, as in a short break between acts.

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer from the Croatian capital is having a hard time finding work.
explanation.definitionFit: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, so a native of that city is a Croatian national.

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Taking part in some community project out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stake or share in some affair, as in declaring a financial concern, is a form of participation.

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A political reform gets the blame for a breakdown of order.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedlam was the London asylum of Bethlem, whose name came to mean uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Total chaos and uproar, a scene with no order or control, is what both words describe.

blocks.note: first meaning: a breed of wild goose, once thought to hatch from shellfish
second meaning: crustaceans that cling to the hulls of boats

explanation.walkthrough: The barnacle goose takes its name from the old belief that it grew out of the shellfish found on driftwood.
explanation.definitionFit: The name serves both a black-and-white Arctic bird and the small marine crustaceans that encrust hulls and piers.

clue.text: In Armenia, Leo is the sign of the slave

indicators.note: in says the wanted letters sit inside the words that follow it

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the two words

explanation.surface: A horoscope claim that in Armenia those born under Leo are marked out for servitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo pretends to be a star sign; it only supplies its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic servant or drudge, someone doing lowly work for another, much like a slave.

clue.text: Bird obviously happy when among sailors

indicators.note: among puts one thing in the midst of others, so a word is placed inside another

blocks.note: someone plainly cheerful is chuckling
jack is an old name for a seaman, here plural
as can mean while or when

explanation.surface: A cheerful bird perches in the rigging with the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: The kookaburra, an Australian kingfisher, is nicknamed this because its call sounds like loud human laughter.

clue.text: Canoeing madly around river reveals inexperience

indicators.note: doing something madly means wildly and without order, so the letters are scrambled
around says the scrambled letters surround another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A novice paddling wildly down the river shows how little they know.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of knowledge or of practical acquaintance with something is what being green and untried amounts to.

clue.text: Where fallen gladiators bit the sand in ancient Rome?

definitions.text: Where fallen gladiators bit the sand in ancient Rome

blocks.clueFragment: Where fallen gladiators bit the sand
blocks.note: surface reading: the place fighters died in combat
setter's reading: the Latin word for sand gives the name of the place, sand being strewn on its floor

explanation.walkthrough: The Latin for sand is the source of the English word for an amphitheatre floor, which was covered in sand to soak up blood.
explanation.definitionFit: The central space of a Roman amphitheatre, where combats took place, is called this, from the sand covering it.

blocks.note: a woman's name
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A woman who is going downhill is just like everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary and representative, a middle-of-the-road example, is what normal or standard describes.

indicators.note: losing its head means a word drops its first letter

blocks.note: glancing is looking quickly

explanation.surface: A college hoping to get rid of its principal.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCING College is an English public school in West Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a well-known independent boarding school on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Jealousy of men vying for success

indicators.note: of here means taken from, so the letters are drawn out of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words
surface padding that completes the picture of rivalry

explanation.surface: Rivals jostling to get ahead are eaten up with resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for success' adds nothing to the wordplay; it completes the picture of rivalry that breeds the feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentful longing for what someone else has is a near synonym of covetousness or jealousy.

clue.text: Italian production for the Diet of Worms?

explanation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was a council held in the German city of Worms; here diet means food and worms are wriggly creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Very thin Italian pasta strands take their name from the Italian for little worms, so they are a worm diet.

blocks.note: surface reading: people getting together somewhere
setter's reading: contradictory terms placed side by side, as in bittersweet

explanation.walkthrough: An oxymoron joins contradictory words, as in deafening silence.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech like living death pairs words of contrary meaning, so contraries are brought together in it.

clue.text: Palm with leaves used to plait

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Palm fronds are woven into braids.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition lifts the surface fact that its huge leaves are indeed used for weaving and thatch.
explanation.definitionFit: The talipot is a tall south Asian fan palm with enormous fronds, used for thatching and once for writing.

definitions.note: a phrase for a verb form: the answer means making things level

blocks.note: first meaning: the part of the day after afternoon
second meaning: making the score level

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it suggests the moment to pay a bill; split, it gives two senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the close of the day and is also the participle of a verb meaning to square or equalise.

blocks.note: first meaning, stressed on the second syllable: to bewitch or delight
second meaning: the side door that delivery people come in by

explanation.walkthrough: A tradesmen's entrance is the side or back door of a big house kept for deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, stressed on its last syllable, it means to cast a spell; as a noun it is a doorway.

blocks.note: surface reading: food stored in the kitchen deep freeze
setter's reading: the frozen sea or polar cold, holding a ship fast

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests frozen peas; the real picture is a vessel trapped in pack ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or harbour hemmed in and immobilised by frozen sea is said to be held fast this way.

clue.text: For this Chopin wrote two volumes

blocks.note: surface reading: the composer produced a pair of books
setter's reading: two degrees of loudness, soft and loud, which make up the instrument's name

explanation.walkthrough: The instrument's full Italian name means soft-loud, two volume levels; Chopin wrote almost entirely for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name of the keyboard instrument joins the Italian words for soft and loud, because its hammers can play at either level.

clue.text: Four keys introduce us to computer

taken as written

explanation.surface: Pressing a few keys gets you started on a PC.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical keys are named A to G, so any of those letters can be a key; keys looks like keyboard keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on wires used for arithmetic is a simple calculating device, a computer in the literal sense.

blocks.note: first meaning: sturdy or robust

blocks.note: surface reading: works for the keyboard instrument at 19
